Subject: Recap + next steps: Deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and isolation questions

Thanks again for your time earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned.

Call highlights (short):
- Finovate is prototyping an LLM-powered customer support summarization + KYC helper.
- Key constraints: PII handling, predictable latency during peak trading hours, and ops isolation for audit teams.
- You're evaluating whether Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool), or Private VPC/on-prem is the right fit.

Specific items we discussed about isolation and SLOs:
- Hosted: shared infra with logical isolation, strong rate limits and quotas, and our standard SLOs (99.9% availability).
- Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pools (no noisy-neighbor interference), configurable throughput and SLA targets, recommended for high-concurrency/low-latency workloads.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed networking and key management, recommended if you need complete data plane control or strict regulatory controls.

Open questions from our side (helps us produce a recommendation):
1) What are your 95th/99th latency goals for inference under peak workload?
2) Do you expect sustained concurrent reqs >500/sec or short bursts above that?
3) Any internal compliance requirement that mandates customer-controlled keys or on-prem data storage?

Proposed next steps:
- Ben (SE) to send a short diagram comparing isolation boundaries for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and answer your noisy-neighbor/SLO questions (by EOD).
- Finovate to share expected QPS and latency targets and any non-functional reqs for compliance by Fri 3/12.
- Follow-up meeting: 30 minutes next week to review recommendation and MAP (proposed 3/16).

Attachments referenced: hosted-vs-dedicated-one-pager.pdf (quick table)

Thanks —

- QPS: baseline 150 qps, peak bursts up to ~800 qps for short windows (market opens).

Hi Emily / Rajesh — Ben from SE here, thanks for the great questions. Short answers and attached diagram (redwood-dedicated-arch.png) + one-pager.

1) Hosted noisy-neighbor risk: Hosted is multi-tenant at the control plane level but we logically isolate workloads and enforce strict rate limits and per-tenant quotas. For small-to-medium production workloads the noisy-neighbor risk is low because:
   - Continuous batching and smart scheduling minimize job preemption.
   - We run per-customer queues and backpressure so a single tenant can't monopolize a GPU.
   - For tail-latency sensitive paths, we have a performance tier routing that pins requests to warmed worker pools.

2) Dedicated: physically reserved GPU pools for your account — eliminates noisy neighbor at the infra level. You get configurable SLOs (we can target tighter 99th percentiles and dedicated throughput).

3) Private VPC/on-prem: full isolation and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). If you require key custody and full audit isolation, this is the recommended path.

Recommendation given your numbers:
- Since you have bursts to ~800 qps with tight 99th targets, Dedicated capacity or a hybrid (Dedicated for peak windows + Hosted for baseline) is likely the best fit. Dedicated removes noisy neighbor risk and lets us set tighter SLOs.
- Key management: Hosted supports customer-managed keys for data-at-rest in our enterprise tier, but Private gives you the most control if your security team insists on on-prem KMS/HSM.

I've attached: redwood-dedicated-arch.png (diagram) and hosted-vs-dedicated-one-pager.pdf. Also linking our SLA page and a short article on isolation patterns.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
